title: MATH GAOKAO - 375
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Divide complex numbers in rectangular form by multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator.
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{3+4i}{1-2i}\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(1+2i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3+4i}{1-2i}&=\frac{(3+4i)(1+2i)}{(1-2i)(1+2i)} \\
&=\frac{3+6i+4i+8i^2}{1^2+2^2} \\
&=\frac{-5+10i}{5} \\
&=-1+2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(-1+2i\).
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.

questions.concept: Division with a Binomial Complex Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Divide a complex number by a binomial complex denominator and simplify the result.
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{2-5i}{3+i}\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(3-i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2-5i}{3+i}&=\frac{(2-5i)(3-i)}{(3+i)(3-i)} \\
&=\frac{6-2i-15i+5i^2}{3^2+1^2} \\
&=\frac{1-17i}{10} \\
&=\frac{1}{10}-\frac{17}{10}i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(\frac{1}{10}-\frac{17}{10}i\).

questions.learningObjective: Divide two complex conjugates and simplify the quotient.
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{1+i}{1-i}\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(1+i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1+i}{1-i}&=\frac{(1+i)^2}{(1-i)(1+i)} \\
&=\frac{1+2i+i^2}{2} \\
&=\frac{2i}{2} \\
&=i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(i\).
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of \(1-i\).

questions.learningObjective: Divide complex numbers and express the quotient in the form \(a+bi\).
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{5+2i}{2-3i}\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(2+3i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{5+2i}{2-3i}&=\frac{(5+2i)(2+3i)}{(2-3i)(2+3i)} \\
&=\frac{10+15i+4i+6i^2}{2^2+3^2} \\
&=\frac{4+19i}{13} \\
&=\frac{4}{13}+\frac{19}{13}i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(\frac{4}{13}+\frac{19}{13}i\).

questions.concept: Division of a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.learningObjective: Divide a real number by a complex number and simplify the quotient.
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{4}{2+i}\).
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(2-i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{4}{2+i}&=\frac{4(2-i)}{(2+i)(2-i)} \\
&=\frac{8-4i}{2^2+1^2} \\
&=\frac{8-4i}{5} \\
&=\frac{8}{5}-\frac{4}{5}i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(\frac{8}{5}-\frac{4}{5}i\).

questions.learningObjective: Divide complex numbers in polar form by dividing moduli and subtracting arguments.
questions.question: Let \(z_1=6(\cos80^\circ+i\sin80^\circ)\) and \(z_2=2(\cos20^\circ+i\sin20^\circ)\). Find \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\).
questions.explanation:
In polar form,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{z_1}{z_2}&=\frac{6}{2}\left(\cos(80^\circ-20^\circ)+i\sin(80^\circ-20^\circ)\right) \\
&=3(\cos60^\circ+i\sin60^\circ).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\cos60^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{z_1}{z_2}&=3\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right) \\
&=\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}i\).
questions.hint: In polar form, divide the moduli and subtract the arguments.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a real parameter so that a complex quotient is real.
questions.question: For what real value of \(a\) is \(\frac{2+ai}{1-i}\) real?
questions.explanation:
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(1+i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{2+ai}{1-i}&=\frac{(2+ai)(1+i)}{(1-i)(1+i)} \\
&=\frac{2+2i+ai+ai^2}{2} \\
&=\frac{(2-a)+(2+a)i}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the quotient to be real, its imaginary part must be zero:
\[
2+a=0 \implies a=-2.
\]
Thus \(a=-2\).
questions.hint: Multiply by the conjugate and set the imaginary part equal to zero.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the modulus of a complex quotient using modulus properties.
questions.question: Let \(z=\frac{1+2i}{3-4i}\). Find \(|z|\).

questions.concept: Solving a Complex Linear Equation by Division
questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear equation involving complex division and express the solution in standard form.
questions.question: If \(z(1+2i)=3-4i\), find \(z\).
questions.explanation:
Divide both sides by \(1+2i\):
\[
z=\frac{3-4i}{1+2i}.
\]
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(1-2i\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
z&=\frac{(3-4i)(1-2i)}{(1+2i)(1-2i)} \\
&=\frac{3-6i-4i+8i^2}{1^2+2^2} \\
&=\frac{-5-10i}{5} \\
&=-1-2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(z=-1-2i\).
questions.hint: Divide both sides by \(1+2i\) and multiply by its conjugate.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a power of a complex number before dividing and express the result in standard form.
questions.question: Compute \(\frac{(1+i)^3}{1-i}\).
questions.explanation:
First simplify the power:
\[
(1+i)^2=2i,
\]
so
\[
\begin{aligned}
(1+i)^3&=(1+i)^2(1+i) \\
&=2i(1+i) \\
&=2i+2i^2 \\
&=-2+2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{(1+i)^3}{1-i}&=\frac{-2+2i}{1-i} \\
&=\frac{(-2+2i)(1+i)}{(1-i)(1+i)} \\
&=\frac{-2-2i+2i+2i^2}{2} \\
&=\frac{-4}{2} \\
&=-2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the quotient is \(-2\).
questions.hint: Simplify \((1+i)^3\) first, then divide by multiplying by the conjugate of \(1-i\).
